newsitem.title: ESTONIA: BOURSE MADE A LOSS OF 427,000 KROONS IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE MADE A LOSS OF 427,000 KROONS IN 1996.

text.p: The Tallinn Stock Exchange's shareholders on Thursday approved its 1996 results, which show a net loss of 427,000 kroons.
The Shareholders also decided to issue 20 new shares to Hansa Investments and Kawe Kapital, Helo Meigas, the bourse's managing director, told Reuters.

It also elected a new council. Its members are Heldur Meerits, vice-president of the Estonian central bank, Ivar Lukk, chairman of Forekspank, Peeter Saks, chairman of Talinvest, Margus Schults, vice-president of Uhispank and Heino Viik, head of Hoiupank's financial division.
The Tallinn Stock Exchange, launched in June 1996, plans to make a profit in 1997, Meigas said.
The bourse has 23 shareholders and the number is expected to grow, she added.
